hotel_name: Hotel Saint Sauveur by WP Hotels
review_text:
Despite the publication and price range this Is 4* is unworthy.
Hotel is completely outdated and in need of renovation.
Upon arrival the room was not cleaned, fingerprints and hairs of the previous hotel guests were abundant, and this during covid period.
The bathroom was completely worn, mold spots in and around the shower and sink, stains on walls and ceilings, taps worn, rusted and completely calcified. Windows hadn't been cleaned for weeks, the handles were literally black with dirt.
The renovation work already carried out looked more like amateurish bricolage than thorough renovation (laminate simply laid over the old fitted carpet, holes in the walls for extra cabling).
When reported to the counter, the friendliness of the staff quickly deteriorated. A cleaning lady was sent on the spot who apparently lacked a special product (= Antical). Unfortunately she was only in possession of a spray with Javel but would certainly report this to the 'Manager'. A good morning from the staff turned out to be no longer an option. However, the hotel apparently has a rather high reputation when it comes to friendliness of the staff.
Despite the multiple positive scores for breakfast, this was also a disappointment.
A very classic and standard breakfast was offered 'corona proof', but if you wanted a glass of cava, each guest had to take the same bottles to pour themselves during covid. Moreover, the waiter on duty didn't speak the Dutch language. The dining room turned out not to be cleaned either, dust and food remains of previous guests were easily spotted.
This is the first time in 20 years that I am writing a review. However, I have never had such a negative experience (not even in countries where the stars are awarded 'smoother').
Any self-respecting 4* hotel would notice these things for themselves and take action here.
Be warned before booking your overpriced room here.

review_text:

Towards an unbearable heat and with the air conditioning not working could not be in the room, for which I had to open the balcony doors throughout the night, resulting in the entry of mosquitoes that "fried" me to bites all the night. Left the hotel 5 hrs after arrival...

Chapter2: i called the reception, explained the situation and now the lady told me she has no clue either, and someone will call in 30 min, as they have too much work to do checking in people... after 1 hr waiting no call followed, so we decided to check the pool. 
Chapter 3: there were no towels available in dressing room, so it took me 20 min to find any living person to ask for them, which also took quite some time to bring after.
Chapter 4: lobby bar tables were not cleaned, as a wine list barmen proposed “french” or “argentinian”,  which was also bad wine btw, so we decided to leave

The manager kindly explained me that 1) they do not have bbq facilities since a long time 2) its not a problem of Dolce what is written on Booking.com in the list 3) no reimbursement is possible, even the one of extra payment for the dog which we made during check-in. Here, to be objective he proposed free breakfast as compensation, but we really did not want to stay anymore
Conclusion: if you are not a group of 100 people to occupy conference hall, the property (which is 4 star hotel btw) does NOT care about customers... anyhow it’s forest (which is the only nice part there), so nowhere to run...
The end.

review_text:
We arrived at 2.35pm to be told our room wasn’t ready and to come back at 3pm. We very much had the impression that the room was ready and they just have a policy of making you wait until the 3pm check in time. When we got our room it had 5 or 6 flies buzzing round, and the sloping walls were thick with dust and dirt. We went down to ask for a different room, and were asked if we had touched anything in the room. I do wonder if we would have been told we couldn’t change rooms if we had in fact touched something. We were then told that the walls weren’t dirty, it was shadow, despite us saying we had brushed some of it off. The man at reception continued to argue, but nevertheless changed our room. We came down later and the man in reception continued to argue, so asked to speak to the manager. He apologised, and offered us late check out. Later that evening we returned and the receptionist did then apologise, but STILL argued that we were wrong and the room wasn’t dirty! The room was also very noisy, we had a poor nights sleep because of the loud shouting on the street.,

Location was good, very close to the Grand Place. There are lots of restaurants and bars nearby. It’s an easy walk from Bruxelles Centrale station.

Bruegel was far from cheap a price close to a hotel without basic service top back it up. So worst stay ever unfortunately.... I never thought this can happen in an European capital - hostel without heating at winter time....,

The location is really good, close to all sights and next to a nice church.

review_title: Advertised facilities not at this property
review_text:
The property was advertised as having 2 bedrooms and 1 bathroom with a hot tub when in fact there was no bathroom only a shower and sink within the main bedroom. This caused major problems for us as we were a group of 4 adults who all needed the use of the shower and sink which could not happen when the bedroom was in use.
The 2nd bedroom is in the attic this is fine for children but being an adult of 6ft meant every time I got out of bed my head banged into the eaves of the wall. This bedroom did not have a wardrobe this was situated on the 1st floor landing which meant coming up and down stairs when clothes were needed.
The property was advertised as having a balcony with city views and a terrace unfortunately this was again incorrect as there is no balcony at this property and the terrace was tiny and was filled with plant pots you could not sit outside. I feel let down as the advertisement for the property sounded great but without these facilities our stay was not comfortable. ,

The welcome we got when we arrive was lovely.
The property was about a 10 minute walk from the centre. 
The downstairs of the house was lovely a great little kitchen with all you needed for your stay. The sitting area was big enough for 4 adults and was comfortable. 
The use if 2 bikes was a nice touch although we did not use them.
If you are a family with young children then this house would be nice for you but a group of adults just doesn't work with out a separate bathroom.

review_text:
To start with, it was very strange that half of the amenities in the hotel were not working because they were broken / unavailable. I have NEVER encountered this in a 5* hotel. For instance, the bathtub in our room was broken - water was not flowing into the bathtub because the pipes were broken or unattached to the tub, for this reason water was flowing below the tub and not in it. We have checked under the tub and the entire space  was wet and mouldy. The shower head was not very well attached (or full of limescale), so the water was flowing outside the shower head and not through it. The shower tile was chipped. In the men's area of the spa,  jacuzzi was not working. How is this acceptable in a 5* hotel???
The staff appears to be not very well trained. Some members of the staff were very nice and helpful while others were downright rude. We have ordered a couple of items from the mini bar; as the mini bar was not filled upon our arrival, the lady came up to our room carrying all the contents of the mini bar. Trying to save her some trouble, I have told her that we only need a couple of items, so there is no need to fill the entire mini bar. She said quite rudely that this is not a restaurant so I cannot order whatever I want and proceeded to fill the entire mini bar. I am pretty sure that she could approached the matter differently. Some staff members do not speak English. If you address them in English they freak out and pass you along to their colleague. When they do speak English, they come out quite rude, e.g. asking "what do you want?" instead of "how can I help you?". Again, the lack of proper training is prominent. I have stayed in similarly priced 5* hotels in other countries and the staff goes above and beyond to ensure quality experience for their guests.
To be fair, we have not tried the breakfast, so maybe it would have improved our experience (breakfast was highly rated among other quests).,

I have very mixed emotions about this hotel. While I liked some aspects of it (beautiful lobby, spacious rooms, down pillows and duvet, cleanliness), some things have really let me down.

review_text:
Carpets in general are always outdated and unhygenic, but this one was covered in unknown stains, all across the room. Reading other people's reviews I realised I was not the only one encountering this. I have never seen something like this in Holland. This is unacceptable for a (4-star) hotel. (see photo)While walking around outside its easy to forget that you're actually in Europe; the hotel is close to a train station; at night there are a lot of drug addicts, homeless and gipsies on the streets, sleeping outside or talking to you if you walk by. They come in big numbers. If you travel by car, especially one having a ''foreign'' license plate, it is highly advised to park it in the hotel garage. This costs you €25. Group of men hang around the parked cars outside, I witnessed one urinating against one. I personally wouldn't go out alone at night as a woman or with children. Be aware of pickpockets too.,

Rooms were very quiet, unlike many others hotels in Brussels. Reception staff spoke Dutch like they're supposed to.Overall, I've learnt that booking a hotel is always quite a gamble in Belgium, even at 4-5 star hotels, the quality standard is lower. However this one was decent enough.

Check out is very easy, you just leave your key in a box and go.

First of all, the service. Girls at the reception didn't want to communicate, nice and I didn't feel welcome to ask any questions or assistance what so ever. I instead used google engine to look for the information instead of talking to them.There was a huge problem with my in-room breakfast. The reception provides you with a card (bad quality printing), with a number of dishes and drinks and no price in it. When I asked about the price upon my arrival, they suggested me to double check in the restaurant. I checked the prices and ordered a breakfast for the next morning. However, I was charged twice of that sum. It turned out that from 7-11 am they charge 25$ for any food ordered upstairs, which was a big surprise. It took me 24 hours to sort this out and the staff was very reluctant to do anything about it.On the friday evening there was a wedding upstairs, so it was very loud and noisy (even though I have requested a quiet room - ladies at the reception offered me to pack my stuff and move to another room at thr midnight). I assume that all the rooms from the 14-15th floor have such a problem. The staff couldn't do anything, so I had to call the reception 2 more times.Do not order drinks at the bar because the wine is not what is seems. I have ordered wine from Chile and it wasn't the one, moreover the bartender added water to the white wine (they use this practice to earn money).,

Overall, the room was nice and it was not far from the Minsk Arena, but I think these are the only advantages of this hotel.

review_text:
I arrived at 19.00 as I had informed the staff previously.  It was raining hard and cold, and the staff had already left (Friday night), but the key code did not work, nor did anyone pick up the phone as per instructions.  Only after calling several times on the external line (from my phone) was my call answered.  However, the person on the line was not familiar with the location nor of the system for checking in, and therefore I was only able to gain access to my room key with the help of another couple who had been at the hotel before.  The room was very nice, but not the best for dogs - access via a narrow spiral staircase (dogs had to be carried). To be fair, it turned out I had been allocated the wrong room.  No doubt wonderful in the summer, and superb for weddings and family holidays, but not ideal for an overnight stay on a cold and wet night.,

Beautiful setting and buildings.  Nicely renovated. Comfortable room and clean.  Very quiet - although the hotel seems quite empty given the time of the year.

I clearly specified in the messages that if I did not receive an answer by 4th 1150 I'll check out and rent something else.

review_text:
This was the last room available near to the Menin Gate that accepted dogs. We would have stayed in the same hotel as my son and family but, unfortunately, they didn't accept pets. Our room was clearly meant for family occupation, having two singles and two bunk beds squashed into a dark and dingy room with a view of a partition wall right outside the window. The bathroom was horrible. The door didn't close fully, the lock had been vandalised and there were other signs of damage in the room. My son and family had breakfast with us on one morning and were charged E20 each although there was no charge for the children.  To be fair - we did glimpse (longingly) the rooms at the front of the hotel which overlooked the Grote Market square and they seemed a lot brighter and more acceptable.     We wouldn't stay again however.,

The proximity to the Menin Gate - we were visiting to lay a wreath for my grandfather who was killed at Passchendaele.   Breakfast wasn't bad and was inclusive.     Cleaning staff were friendly.

review_title: It's ok just for one night, but we wouldn't come back
review_text:
When we arrived at the hotel, at around 6 p.m., we didn't find anyone welcoming us at the reception: there were only different keys on the table for different guests (to be honest, anyone could have entered the hotel and picked them up from the table because there was literally no one...). In fact, we picked up our key and at first we stepped on the wrong strairs, so we had to go search for our room (it would have been useful to know this information from the receptionist).When we entered the room and the bathroom, we could tell that they were clean: too bad that when we opened the toilet lid, there was some toilet paper in the WC (maybe it was a mistake, but it was disgusting to see it).The worst thing was that, after taking a shower, a smell of sewer came out of the shower (we did not feel at ease after this).The next morning my boyfriend kindly explained in French to the owners of the hotel (a young guy and a man) that we found strange not seeing anyone at the check-in, and they answered that it was our mistake because we said that we would have come in the morning (the check-in time is between 3-9 p.m., as shown on booking.com, so we thought it wouldn't have been a problem); anyway, the young guy was very nice with us and apologised, while the older one was not.We also kindly asked if it was possible to leave them the luggage for some time before leaving, and they said yes and that they would have been around all day, but when we came back to pick up the luggage no one was there.,

The hotel is in a very good position, it's exactly in the main square of Durbuy. The view is also very good, we could see the castle from our window. The room and the bathroom were clean and the breakfast was good, my boyfriend and I spent Easter in this hotel and we found different types of Easter eggs in the tray. It was very lovely!

review_title: Pretty Place Ruined by Owner/Chef with anger management issues.
review_text:
The owner/chef Wim(?), ruined our time at this location.  He is a hot head with a chip on his shoulder that ended up being the downfall of our time there as well as two Americans also staying there that we befriended.  As John Paul, our Belgian American friend said "this guy is really bad for Belgium."  Not to prolong the misery but the incident arose after we were gifted by Van Steenberg Brewery near Ghent a magnum of our favorite Belgium beer, Tripel de Garre.  We told the staff we wanted to share it with others and the young son showed us we had a fridge in our room.  I then told Wim we met their guests from America and wanted to get some cheeses to offer them when we shared the bottle. Wim directed me to the store.  We met our friends on the public patio outside well away from the B&B and restaurant.  there was no one in the bar or restaurant.  I asked the young worker if we could use four glasses to share the beer and he graciously agreed.  After about 30 minutes of quietly enjoying the view and the beer, Wim stormed onto the public patio, told us we were not allowed to drink our belgium beer there and insisted we leave immediately.  We said OK and started to gather our belongings but Wim shouted "right now, you must leave immediately!" He then claimed in 20 years no guest has ever had the audacity to share a beverage on the public patio.  At that point, we had to ask him to calm down as he was acting threatening, but the rant continued.  He even told us about the size of his mortgage as if drinking our gift had deprived him of significant value!  The said thing is our simple celebration with new found friends is not what is depriving him of income.  It is the atrociously sophomoric culinary experience he offers.  It was also the low light of our eating in Belgium.  This guy really should not be in the service or culinary business.  To prove the point, aside from the four of us, only one other couple ever showed up for dinner.,

The place is up a steep hill but accessible if you've got stamina or a car.  The views, especially from our room #2 were dramatic of the city and the Count's Fort.  It had a lovely "public patio" (quotes to be explained later) and our room also had a grand outdoor patio.

hotel_name: Holiday Inn Hasselt, an IHG Hotel
review_text:
The beds were not comfortable and the room really needed renovation (currently undergoing). The room had a fire alarm with a light,  which was blinking all night long. The room and the bathroom were very cold. The noise from the renovation started at around 9.00 am on a Saturday. The spa area was not well done - only one shower; no separate area to shower or cool down after the sauna; swimming pool is very small and the whole area was very cold. The underground parking entrance was really tight and the tariff is 16 euros (regardless of the time spent in the parking). We had a problem when trying to exit because our ticket (which we had paid at the reception) was not accepted by the machine and the barrier did not open. After turning around several times in the parking, going back to the reception, which could not help, and looking for a way to contact somebody responsible for the parking, we tried again and it worked this time.,

The staff was very nice and helpful. The room is a good size and the location is convenient. The wellness centre (swimming pool, sauna and gym) are free but are not well done (see the comments below) and need renovation. The hotel is currently being renovated so hopefully the wellness area will also be redone. The room service for breakfast was really good and the service in the restaurant was excellent (the food was pretty basic though).

review_text:
The rooms facing the main road and down the side were noisy from traffic, people but, above all, from several trams that only stop for a few hours at night and that ring a bell as they go up and down the road. 
The hotel was very busy and the pool and bar area were often too busy for their own good. The pool is a lovely touch but so small as to be little more than a place to cool down if really hot. 
One staff member contradicted me several times when I mentioned our room was noisy, even asking me why I thought the rooms at the back would be quieter (p.s. we moved to one on the second night and they were quieter, by a long shot!) She also told me that the endless and louder than loud trams were just 'the normal noise of a city' and generally talked back at me as if I were an annoyance instead of a paying customer. Having just had to pay upfront for our room, I didn't appreciate this at all.
Breakfast was ok but not impressive and the staff was unhelpful. You fry your own eggs on a hot plate. Very odd 
Some rooms were hot. There is no air con but you get a fan. In some rooms the windows don't open. ,

The vibe was cool and the retro design in the rooms well done. The pool, though small, is a nice touch and the area around and it and panoramic bar upstairs are genuinely pleasant. 
The beds were comfortable and the showers were excellent. 
The location was good and well connected.
The coffee was good though if you want hot milk you have to heat your own milk on the coffee machine using the steamer (don't expect the staff to help).
One of the receptionists was very nice and helped us change room very efficiently

review_title: Not 3 star accommodation - basic essentials missing, you'd get better vfm elsewhere
review_text:
Have to say, I don't normally write hotel reviews but felt like I had to with this one. So much could have been better really and it wouldn't take much..We had a deluxe double room but it was so basic. All the basic amenities were missing. There was no safe, kettle, pictures on the walls, the towels (and I don't normally notice things like this) were so thin and small, literally wouldnt use these on my dog! The air con doesn't really work. There were only 2 hangers in the room, when we asked they gave us 2 more but when we said 4 between us might not be enough the manager said there were more coming next week - fair enough but the total of all these things just made us feel like the standard wasn't quite good enough for the £589 we paid for 3 nights I couldn't believe we were made to pay not only for hot drinks but for hot water..!! 2 euros 50 per cupWhen you walked in the room, ive never felt this before but it was a disappointment and have to say as it was our first time in Bruges/Belgium let down the holiday a bit. There's no pictures on the walls and nothing in/on the units - it just feels a bit basic. We didn't sample the breakfast so can't comment on that. The bathroom was small ish - smaller than the pictures but nice enough The hotel interior on the hallways or the floors definitely needed a bit of an update, I'd read reviews on here which said that but didn't expect it to be so prominent - its noticeable and overall you just feel like it wouldn't take much to update these things but money must be being invested elsewhere?,

Location was good - you are only a few mins walk from the main shops/restaurants and right by the Interparking t'zand so extremely convenient. The parking only costs 8 euros overnight so thats great and you literally come out of the parking and the hotel's on your right Staff on reception were friendly and often happy to chat, but often refused the most basic of requests, such as making us pay 2 euro 50 for hot water (we'd bought our own tea bags and milk)

review_title: Tired looking and no comfort, undeserving of its 3 stars
review_text:
The hotel lacks soul and the rooms and decor  are tired looking and outdated. Tile floors in the rooms make it cold and unpleasant. In fact, heating was off and the room freezing when we arrived, which definitely doesn't make for a welcoming feel. And about feeling welcome, there's a warning at every wall or in the lifts or at breakfast: hospitality does not in any way seem to be on the owners' /managers' minds at all. Towels are washed out grey or yellow, rather than white. The mattress felt like cardboard and foam blocks serve as pillows, preventing a good night's sleep. Breakfast was meagre with low quality cold cuts and cheese, old bread and a lady (owner?) shouting after you where stuff is, therefore not allowing for a quiet, relaxing breakfast (it's not included anyway, so you're better off going somewhere nice). Having travelled a lot, we had a laugh with how bad the hotel was and we only stayed 1 night, so it was doable. But it baffled us how a place like this can have 3 stars. ,

The hotel being situated on the river side, close to the cute old town really is it's only good point.

Fortunately only spent one night at La Chaumiere. Am sorry to say that the negatives outweigh the positives. Arrived after a 600 km drive arrived only to find roadworks prevented access to hotel. Workmen suggested return 2 hrs later but finally after staff remonstrated with workmen we gained access to hotel. Had booked family room for 2 adults and 2 children. Attic room up 2 flights of stairs (no lift). One side of landing room contained Large double and single with small box room other side of landing and bathroom off. Rooms very clean but rather tired. Fortunately I was able to negotiate stairs despite being disabled, but anyone with greater disabilities or mobility issues would struggleThe restaurant menu was fine but not suitable for an 8 and 10 yr old. No child options. Having travelled to visit relatives we were OK as they took us to restaurants that had child friendly menu. The room was described as having tea and coffee making facilities and mini bar. Tea and coffee provided but no milk and minibar was an empty fridge barely cool. Single beds lumpy and more put you up that anything elseThe bathroom sink waste did not work so running water only and partially used toiletries were available with a pre-used (ie wet) face cloth (ugh). Towels were provided but again rather tired. The shower attachment in the bath barely did the job and useless. It felt as though room not prepared properlyBreakfast was very basic, however coffee was only available by the cup and had to be requested for refill. Despite 4 requests for hot water for tea non arrived.The hotel might be ok for a travelling rep but I would not rate it as the 3* rating. I have stayed in B&B in area at smaller cost. Perhaps the issue with the breakfast was due to a limited grasp of English or possibly because the staff had attention on breakfast tv. On the whole disappointing, not as described, and sorry  but when returning to area later in year will not be booking La Chaumiere.,

review_text:
The reason people book hotels for their time away from home is to have a roof over their heads and an opportunity to wash themselves. Motel One somehow almost failed both these basic tourist needs for us. Yes, “almost” is the key word here, but the mood and first impression were ruined.
I’ll tell you my story. The day before our booking date I receive an email from booking.com saying my credit card is invalid (my bad, forgot to update it before the trip). It says that unless I updated it within 24 hours, my booking will be cancelled. No big deal, I update it within an hour after the email. In the app my status is changed to “booking confirmed” again. Guess what happened at the front desk? That’s right: they cancelled my damn booking. Absolutely not willing to help and looking at my CONFIRMED booking in the app he doesn’t even apologize. The only room available on the spot is business suite. It seems I don’t have another choice - I pay for business suite: this was about “almost no roof over my head”. What if I was a traveler on budget? What if I simply didn’t have enough money? Not their problem.
Cherry on top to the check-in: it was towards midnight and THERE WAS A LINE for check-in. We waited for 25 minutes only to learn that we’ve been cancelled.
Another cherry: they blamed Booking.com for not sending an email about cancellation (remember this, it’s important for later).
What’s up with lines at midnight? I’ll tell you. The hotel is HUGE. It’s enormous. And only TWO people and the front desk. In our case they called a third one, but it was still 25+ minutes. For this very reason don’t expect special treatment (not even a smile!) because you are not special when there are hundreds of guests.
The shower thing. One morning it turns they don’t have hot water. Just no hot water. For me this was strike two. No phones in the room so we go downstairs to ask. As expected, there are a lot of people waiting (in the line, of course) to be explained. Pipes, they say.

review_text:
Highly advertised location but promises just promises – as matter of fact a ‘never to return establishment’ – unless you fancy the stench of cow dung first thing in the morning when opening the window.  Upon entering the Guesthouse your first experience will be painful (and continues to get worse) – door frames are perfect for people < 180 cm. I am just 185cm and constantly banged my head somewhere. We had a family room consisting of two bedrooms (Master and Children). The beams in the ‘child’s room’ were 183cm high, in the master room 179cm. No hazard tape anywhere! Good paper listed choice of breakfast – in reality the selection of cheese or ham or jam was precision measured. For each slice of bread half a slice of above mentioned.
Other example: - standard boiled egg (anywhere in the world eggs are boiled hard for sanitary reasons), here so soft as if the hen just dropped it and therefore saved the Hosts the effort to heat up some water.
Our family room (though we booked it as a couple without children) was advertised and presented so with a sauna. You may guess by now: Fake news!
Yes, there is a 2 person home built sauna on the second floor – but only available from 5pm to 7 pm and extra charge of 5E p/p. This is for the sauna only – not even having a tub nor shower.
Major highlight was our last day in this location:
We were told that one of the beds is needed for a family of five arriving soon.
Upps, within minutes the bed was gone….. I want to say that we reserved and paid consciously for a family room for us as a couple without kids, as it was largest room available (with sauna advertised) at time of booking.
Sorry for my sarcasm, but it best describes this location. The hosts perfected the art of saving any nickel and dime while attempting to appear the best ***in the area.
They also have own Farm products for sale like cheese and marmalade etc…. Be aware, I bought one marmalade to complement the (precision measured breakfast) jam.,

Nothing really – location is what it is: a one horse village in middle of nowhere – next available Supermarket (lol: a ‘Grandma’s convenience store’ at best) is miles away.

review_title: The property has seen better days
review_text:
Flat 401 where we stayed looked quite shabby and in need of renovation which has not been done for a some time. Marks, scuffs, scratches, on the walls and ceiling, holes from old fixtures, signs of wear and tear everywhere, gray towels, discolored old sofa with the disfigured armrest - all this does not take much to repaint and refresh now and then, yet has not been done for a while. The access to the property with several long flights of stairs is not easy and friendly for people carrying small children or heavy luggage, so travel light!  Also if traveling by car to this very central location, beware of the Low Emission Zone introduced in Antwerpen in 2017, which requires special authorization for foreign cars (advance application online) - something the host never mentioned when advising on the nearest car park in the central Antwerpen.,

Very responsive host, easy Check-in which can be done any time independent of e.g. late arrival. Generally this could be a nice and comfortable flat benefitting from very central location, however its run-down condition was disappointing.
